questions.q: Why is the built-in Account Owner field hidden on our record pages?
o: It reads as Stephen on nearly everything, so it is misleading
It was replaced by the Case owner field
It is only visible to administrators
questions.e: It was deliberately hidden during the 1 July 2026 view overhaul so nobody derives ownership from it. Sales Rep is the truth.

questions.q: Which of these can Customer Operations resolve alone, with no approval?
o: Giving a customer a discount to win the order
Agreeing 30 day credit terms for a new account
Giving stock and lead times from Intact and chasing a courier
Issuing a credit note as a goodwill gesture
questions.e: Stock, lead times, supplier and courier chasing, order confirmations, standard quotes within the rules and standard returns are all resolve-alone. Discounts and credit terms need sales approval; new credit accounts and larger credit notes need management.

questions.q: Which sidebar entry holds the businesses the equipment is ultimately for?
questions.e: Companies are who we sell to. End Customers are who the kit is for, so competing resellers' deals can roll up under one of them.

questions.q: Why does the document number go in the email subject?
o: So the customer can find it
It is how the email links to the right CRM record and the right Intact document
questions.e: It is the primary linking method between the inbox, the CRM and Intact — the cheapest, most reliable join we have.

questions.q: Why do we insist on the Intact document number in the email subject?
o: It is how CRM activity and the ERP transaction record are tied together
questions.e: Intact owns money and documents; the CRM owns relationships and control. The document number in the subject is the join between the two, so a mistyped or missing number breaks the link.

questions.q: A brand new logo has been created but has not ordered yet. What Account Status?
questions.e: Prospect until the first order lands, then Active. Dormant and Lapsed are accounts that used to trade and stopped.

questions.q: How quickly should a new inbound customer item be acknowledged?
o: Within 1 working hour, or 15 minutes if it is urgent
By the end of the day
questions.e: Acknowledge within 1 working hour, 15 minutes for an urgent operational problem. The first meaningful response follows within 4 working hours.

questions.q: Which of these can you NOT do through the API on our version of the CRM?
o: Build a dashboard, star a favourite or reorder the sidebar
questions.e: Dashboards are read-only through the API on our version, and favourites and sidebar order cannot be set that way either. They have to be built by hand in the browser.

questions.scenario: You have chased a supplier twice about a lead time for a case that is now three days old. There is still no reply, and the customer has a deadline this week.
o: Set the status to Resolved since there is nothing more you can do
Leave the case in In Progress and wait for the supplier to come back
Keep it Waiting – Supplier with the supplier named in Supplier dependency, tick Escalated, set a fresh next action and date, and update the customer even though nothing has changed
Close the case and open a new one when the supplier replies
questions.e: Waiting – Supplier with the vendor named is what makes the watch-list work. Escalate early — blocked and at risk of missing a customer deadline is exactly the trigger. And the customer still gets an update on the promised interval; supplier-dependent items get one every 24 to 48 hours. Resolved means the customer's issue is actually sorted.
